title: 1960s NASA electrostatic accidents: spin test facility and Apollo fire

tellings.quote: So, there was an incident that trapped 11 people in a spin test facility um where they accidentally set off a rocket, a solid rocket and uh there were some casualties there. So, we also had the Apollo fire that you've heard about. So, we've lost I think 14 people to electrostatics at NASA.

plain: In the 1960s at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, static electricity is said to have caused deadly accidents: one set off a solid rocket by mistake and trapped 11 people inside a spin test facility, with some killed, and the fire in the Apollo moon programme is counted as another. A NASA scientist named Charles Buhler tells this, passing on what he learned inside the agency, and says NASA has lost about 14 people to electrostatics in all. He tells it to show how powerful and dangerous electric charge can be, which matters to his own work on propulsion.
